newsitem.title: UK: London stocks hit peak, rest of Europe falls.
newsitem.headline: London stocks hit peak, rest of Europe falls.

text.p: London stocks hit record levels for the second straight day on Wednesday as fears receded of further interest rate hikes but other European bourses were dragged down by a poor start on Wall Street.

On currency markets, worries about central bank intervention gnawed at the dollar, pulling it down by 1.5 yen, its lowest level in more than a month. Sterling was calm after its exuberant jump in reaction to Tuesday's British interest rate hike.
London soared nearly one percent to 4,562.0 in morning trade, bettering the previous intra-day record set on Tuesday, before falling back slightly on New York's negative opening.
Frankfurt floor trade finished down by nearly 0.5 percent after hitting peaks yesterday. After-hours trading on the IBIS index fell sharply, as did Paris, after New York's early losses.

London managed to keep most of its gains as investors savoured stability after recent election uncertainty and optimism triggered by the new Labour government's landmark decision to grant the Bank of England freedom to set interest rates.
Wall Street's near 13 percent jump over the past four weeks also boosted market sentiment but dealers said the blue-chip FTSE index may be vulnerable if heavy profit-taking in New York sets in.
"The FTSE still looks like it has a lot further to go but we might take a breather over the next couple of days," the head of trading at a large brokerage said.
Behind London's big gains on Wednesday were weaker-than-expected output figures which calmed fears that the Bank of England might be tempted to push interest rates higher again in the near future.
Though finance minister Gordon Brown's reform of the British central bank was well received by the markets, some investors had started to become edgy about the direction on interest rates.
The anxiety was caused by the fact that sterling has risen 19 percent on a trade-weighted basis since August. The weak data showed that the rampant pound was hitting Britain's exporters.

News that manufacturing output and industrial production both fell 0.1 percent in March compared with expectations of a 0.3 percent rise helped to dampen speculation about another quick rise in interest rates.
In Frankfurt, floor trade ended down 16.30 points at 3551.98, depressed by Wall Street and as the approach of Thursday's Ascension Day holiday sapped investor interest.
"Nobody wants to make a bet right now," said a Frankfurt dealer. "This is not a day for testing any records."

Paris pre-holiday trade, up 0.4 percent in the morning session, turned sour as investors took profits ahead of the Ascension day holiday and because of some uncertainty about election opinion polls in the next few days.
"It's mainly people squaring up ahead of the long weekend," a dealer said.

In currencies, the dollar fell against the yen as a market already jittery over intervention was spooked by a Japanese news report that Japan, the U.S. and Germany were exploring the possibility of selling dollars for yen.

"What's been said about intervention has always been that if the dollar's coming down the Bank of Japan will give it a helping hand," said Richard Hill, head of FX trading at Bank of America in London. "People are nervous."
The dollar fell to 124.78 in mid afternoon as the market digested the report from Japanese news agency Kyodo. As the dollar weakened against the yen, it drifted down below 1.72 marks.

The Bank of Japan declined to comment on the report, which quoted an international monetary source as saying the intervention talk followed an accord -- reached at the recent G7 meeting -- to cooperate in the currency markets.

Elsewhere, sterling was virtually unchanged on the dollar but slightly down against the mark after Tuesday's excitement, standing at $1.6376 and 2.8146 marks at midafternoon versus $1.6372 and 2.8185 in late Europe yesterday.
STOCKS PRICES AT 1430 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 22.9 points at 4,542.2.
The Paris CAC-40 index was down 11.76 points at 2,640.17.
Frankfurt's DAX index closed down 16.30 points at 3,551.98.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7186 marks compared with 1.7229 marks late in Europe on Tuesday. It was at 124.78 yen, compared to 126.44.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $341.10 an ounce, compared to Tuesday's close in London of $342.85. Silver was $4.74, down one cent.
